Hi Ola — thanks for the forecast and the thoughtful questions. Looping in Kimberly (pricing) and Marissa (dedicated ops) to scope an answer.

High level recommendation for the 3-month pilot:
- Baseline: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool (mix to support burst to 6 GPUs), configured with dynamic burst lanes to handle short peaks to 120 concurrent sessions.
- Autoscale floor: keep a hot pool sized for 40 qps steady-state, burst capacity on demand up to the 6 GPU limit.
- KV cache hit target and batching rules should reduce long-run token consumption by ~18% vs naive per-request execution.

On price protection: we can propose a tiered rebate/credit structure rather than an indexing clause for a short pilot. For longer commitments we offer indexed triggers tied to a GPU cost index with defined discount bands — but that requires legal and finance approval. Kimberly — can you outline the acceptable approval thresholds and what level of discount requires exec sign-off?

I attached a draft mutual action plan with sizing and milestones. Happy to jump on a quick call with procurement.

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

Ola / team — thanks for the context. Quick pricing framework we can offer for pilot -> reserved conversion: 

- Pilot (3 months): standard pilot discount (15% off list) applied to committed baseline (the 4 GPU baseline). No indexation for pilots.
- Conversion path to reserved (12 months): we can offer a stepped protection ladder:
  * If GPU market input cost delta <= +10% vs baseline, no adjustment.
  * If delta between +10% and +20%, customer receives a credit equal to 50% of the incremental pass-through cost, capped at 7% of monthly invoice.
  * If delta > +20%, trigger escalation to Finance/RevOps for case-by-case rebate or indexation (exec approval required).

Approval thresholds: discounts or credits that reduce revenue by >18% require VP-level approval; any contractual indexation (formula in SOW) requires Legal + Revenue Ops review (3–5 business days).

David — can you confirm the exec approval path and roughly how long we should expect for a >20% trigger decision?

Kimberly
Director, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Ola — ops notes and a slight tweak on sizing:

- Recommend we codify a two-stage activation: Stage 1 (pilot weeks 0–4) provision 4 GPUs with aggressive KV caching and warm workers. Stage 2 (weeks 5–12) evaluate real peak utilization; if sustained above 80% of burst lanes, auto-activate the 2 additional GPUs in the pool.
- For the short pilot, we can avoid a formal indexation clause; instead include a committed-notice clause that gives Strata a unilateral right to pause growth for 30 days if our input cost pass-through exceeds the +15% band. That is operationally feasible and avoids contract complexity.

Operational constraints: burst beyond the 6-GPU hard cap will need temporary transient capacity on shared fleet (slightly higher latency). If Strata needs guaranteed headroom above 6 GPUs we should move to a Dedicated Reserved 12-month profile.

Marissa
Head of Dedicated Operations
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Jonas — agreed on the framework. Clarifications from Finance: 

- Anything that creates recurring credits greater than 10% of ARR impact needs VP Finance notification; recurring reductions >18% need CFO approval. For a pilot-to-reserved conversion we typically cap contractual credits to a one-quarter true-up for the first year.
- If we include an indexed SOW, RevOps will need a formula and a monthly reconciliation report (we can provide a template); legal lead time ~5 business days.
- For the >20% shock case, we will convene an exec review within 72 business hours (we need data from procurement/legal to evaluate).

I'll sign off on the staged pilot structure and the pause clause as an interim risk mitigant. Jonas — please confirm you want me to authorize the 15% pilot discount formal offer and I'll route the finance note.

Thanks,
